correctness.rationale: The two experiments are separate, so only the A/B and C/B payoff submatrices matter. Under random replacement the common reproduction/target factor cancels from T_i^-/T_i^+, leaving exp(-w times mutant payoff advantage). Taking first differences in the absorption recurrence and summing up to the fixed boundary at i=6 gives the reciprocal-fixation denominator. Independent exact reconstruction gives prefix sums (-4,-4,0,8,20) and (3,4,3,0,-5), hence D_A=2+2z^4+z^-8+z^-20 and D_C=2+2z^-3+z^-4+z^5. Termwise subtraction verifies z^20(D_A-D_C)=P(z). Exact replay by substitution gave P(1)=0, P'(1)=-15, P(6/5)=3174820597963420709/298023223876953125>0, P(2)=-323583. Three Descartes variations and disjoint brackets at 1, (1,6/5), (6/5,2) exhaust the positive roots counting multiplicity, so the crossings are simple. The fixation difference is -P/(z^20 D_A D_C), giving the stated ordering and neutrality tie. The frozen checker was read, not run. The reported decimal refinements are illustrative; the exact brackets, rather than an independent decimal refinement, were used to certify all positive-selection regimes.

value.rationale: The witness tests a natural inference about using weak- and strong-selection rankings to screen rare invaders of the same resident. Both ends favor the same mutant, yet a whole intermediate interval favors its competitor. The exact two-crossing result establishes the failure in a fixed elementary model without conflating mutant identity with an update rule, invasion site, or coexisting mutant dynamics.
